American healthcare the most expensive on earth, yet failing at an unprecedented pace

To fix it, all they have to do is reform the Malpractice panels.

The Insurance companies have really fucked us over. Here is how it went (for some background, I helped run a small practice. A good chunk of this is first hand.).

Back in the day, insurance was a luxury. Then, they took the drug dealer route. Made it cheap for everyone.

They then lobbied a few things most important was that an insurance company could not be charged more or less than an individual for a service.

They then created Insurance panels-a directory of 'preferred healthcare providers'. This would later be expanded into the PPO setup. But, being on a panel is important. Aside from a provider being excluded in a PPO, a large chunk of people don't have a primary care physician. The list directs customers.

Then, add in malpractice panels-the first phase consists of a basic sort of litmus: "Did the provider in question do the same treatments considered normal within the region they practice in?". I will come back to this part.

Insurance company panels have a contract where in the provider agrees to a write off of a percentage. This is usually fairly high. They also implemented a standard of care and treatment.

Two of the most important effects of this are: Aspirin is charged at $5 a pill because of the write off, they get significantly lower. Second is the flowchart of diagnosis. You can have an obvious compound fracture. However if the doctor doesn't do X-Rays and other portions. Insurance requires people on their panels to do those diagnostics. If you (who are not on that panel) do NOT do that X-Ray, and any question comes up. The malpractice panel will ask 'would others in the area have done it different'? Bam, red mark on license.

Combined: Insurance companies have made it so a long line of diagnostics are required and they pay a fraction of what an uninsured person pays. Treatment costs skyrocket because of the insurance write-off (you've seen it on every bill: Bill amount $1000, write off $950 amount owing $15 for co-pay). Doctors who don't sign these contracts get screwed. They get screwed if they don't because the insurance directs patients to other practices.

This is how monopolies and collusive businesses destroy things. Like crack dealers clamping down.

Edit to add: If they reform the malpractice panels-then practices can cut expensive diagnostic procedures without risk, they can deny taking insurance and simply charge a massive discount for cash rates (they currently have a same day cash pay loophole, but how many without insurance can pay upfront even for a discount?).
